finding: Avg 11.4 revenue orders and ₹8.4 L gross profit per month (CV 41%). STL seasonal strength 0.62, trend strength 0.17, but estimated from fewer than 3 yearly cycles, so any seasonality is unconfirmed. Best month on average: Mar, weakest: Nov. Weekday mix chi-square p=0.51 (no weekday effect).
AOV ranges ₹2.4 L-₹3.1 L by quarter. Correlation of log AOV with units/order 0.70 vs with net price/unit 0.67: AOV moves mainly with basket size (units). Discount rate range 7.4%-12.2%.
Of buyers observed long enough, 10% order again within 90 days, 20% within 180 days, 34% within 365 days. Cohort sizes shrink from 32 buyers/quarter in 2023 to 7 in the last 4 quarters.

Median gap 1st→2nd order 254 days (IQR 131-527). KM probability of a 2nd order: 10% by 90 d, 20% by 180 d, 35% by 1 yr, 54% by 2 yrs. 38% of second orders come after a year, so 'lost' should not be declared before ~12 months of silence.

New buyers by year: {2023: 128, 2024: 64, 2025: 28}. Sign-ups (join_date) by year: {2022: 113, 2023: 123, 2024: 64}; the last sign-up is 25 Sep 2024, with none in the following 13 months. New buyers track sign-ups, so the drop is a top-of-funnel problem (or an extract cut-off), not a conversion problem. 80 registered customers are still unconverted. Repeat orders rose from 17% to 75% of orders.

80 never-ordered customers. Median age 44 vs 43 for buyers (p=0.57); segment difference p=0.56. Top states: {'Maharashtra': 18, 'Gujarat': 11, 'Karnataka': 8}. They look like buyers demographically: non-conversion is not explained by profile.
Champions: 33 customers, 31% of profit. At-risk (2+ orders, not recent): 35 customers holding 21% of profit. Lapsed one-timers: 73. List saved to output/rfm_segments.csv for targeting.

Base repeat rate 58% (n=186). Features significant at p<0.05: none. Logistic regression on first-order features: cross-validated AUC 0.42 (±0.11). Close to random: first-order attributes do not predict repeat buying; retention must be earned after the first order.
Repeat rate 57% with a discounted first order vs 67% without (p=0.75); first-order margin 26.2% vs 33.2%. Discounts do not measurably change repeat behaviour, but they do cost margin.

Top 20% of products earn 49% of gross profit; 91 of 200 products (46%) make 80%. Profit is spread fairly evenly (no strong 80/20). 1 product(s) net loss-making overall. Top subcategory Serum (₹22.3 L); bottom Dumbbell Set (₹4.9 L).

84% of orders span 2+ categories (avg 2.6). Lift ranges 0.92-1.05; all near 1, so categories are bought independently. No natural cross-sell pair stands out; bundles would need to be designed, not discovered.
Largest mix difference: Beauty +5.5 pp for recurring, Fashion -3.1 pp. Differences are small: recurring customers buy the same mix, just more often.
Margin falls from 0% to 15% item discount in every category: biggest drop Fashion (16.2 pp), smallest Home & Kitchen (8.7 pp). Erosion is broadly uniform, so a single discount cap policy fits.
Top states by profit: Maharashtra 22%, Gujarat 18%, Karnataka 9%. Highest profit per customer (n>=8): West Bengal (₹1.8 L); lowest: Tamil Nadu (₹1.0 L). Repeat rate differs by state p=0.43.
Cancel/return rate by method 0.0%-6.4% (chi-square p=0.57, not significant). Cash on Delivery: 16 orders, 0% cancelled - COD is not riskier here.
Profit per customer by age group ₹1.1 L-₹2.0 L (Kruskal p=0.11); repeat rate by gender 48%-57%. Groups are small (18-24 has 19 buyers); no demographic is a reliable targeting lever.
Wholesale: 41 buyers, repeat 49%, ₹1.3 L/customer; Retail: 179 buyers, repeat 54%, ₹1.3 L/customer (p=0.93). The segments behave alike; the label carries little signal.
